name: Adrian Dias
life: “I still remember disliking my nickname long before I learned its origin.” On Tuesday, near Maré Coffee, Adrian likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I hate the fictional nickname. I brought the author the one the children actually gave me.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a charcoal zip cardigan and a watch on a cracked leather band. Adrian has a round face with a pronounced chin, with tightly curled gray hair. Adrian gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in during a conversation.
personality: Adrian has a strong competitive streak and a very soft spot for the person finishing last. A prize tastes better when everybody had enough time to enter.
agenda: To let the author hear the nickname actually used.
family: Maeve Hamm is Adrian’s cousin raised in the same household. Adrian brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Maeve makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The quiet verse*, Maeve says, “I heard the fountain through that gap. I've lived beside it for years and never knew it had two rhythms.”
connections: Josephine Fields. A mother's widely told story sounds different in the real person's preferred words.

reactions.situation: A reader asks the real person to autograph the novel
reactions.response: Adrian gives the customer a graceful way to decline the autograph.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Adrian brings the worker into the conversation and asks what they remember without feeding them a story.

reactions.response: Adrian explains exactly what help was offered and offers the same practical help to the accuser.
